newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PM defends Australia's foreign aid spending.
newsitem.headline: PM defends Australia's foreign aid spending.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard on Monday defended his government's A$1.4 billion (US$1.1 billion) annual foreign aid budget, which critics say could be better used fighting unemployment.

"I think the present level of foreign aid is right, both in terms of Australia's national interest and also in terms of the humanitarian obligations this country has as a relatively wealthy country..." Howard told parliament.
Howard's conservative government, facing unemployment stuck at around 8.5 percent, is under increasing pressure to cut foreign aid and redirect the money to job-creation schemes.

Howard said Australia had a moral obligation to help poorer countries, but added there was "an obligation on governments and all political parties to make absolutely certain that foreign aid is directed in the most efficient manner".
Howard called for "political pressure" on countries that have intolerable regimes or which use starvation and the wasting of civilian populations as a method of achieving their goals.
"We should never be reluctant to condemn that sort of behaviour," Howard said.

"The answer is not to turn our back on foreign aid. Our answer is to try and get a more effective aid delivery system...that returns optimum benefits to the Australian people while discharging our humanitarian obligations."
Most Australian aid goes to countries in the Asia-Pacific region.
